proposals.before: The Xiang–Wei six-prefecture circuit received the title Zhaoyi Army circuit; later Tian Chengsi seized four of its prefectures, leaving only two.
proposals.after: The Xiang–Wei six-prefecture circuit received the title Zhaoyi Army circuit; later Tian Chengsi seized Xiang, Wei, Ming, and Bei prefectures—four in all—leaving only two.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits the four prefecture names that the Chinese and literal fields explicitly list (相、衛、洺、貝).

proposals.before: The Youzhou deputy military commissioner concurrently led the Pinglu Army deputy military commissioner, with seat at Shunhua Prefecture.
proposals.after: The Youzhou deputy military commissioner concurrently served as Pinglu Army deputy military commissioner, with seat at Shunhua Prefecture.
proposals.reason: Literal English unnaturally says he 'led' the deputy office itself; 領 here means he concurrently held that deputy commissionership.

proposals.before: The Youzhou circuit concurrently served as frontier commissioner of its home prefecture and army, and also as grand commissioner over all Hebei forces.
proposals.after: The Youzhou military commissioner concurrently served as frontier commissioner of his home prefecture and army, and also as grand commissioner over all Hebei forces.
proposals.reason: Literal English treats the Youzhou circuit as the officeholder; the Chinese 幽州節度 refers to the military commissioner, as the idiomatic field correctly renders.

proposals.before: An observation commissioner for Ping, Ying, Mo, and neighboring prefectures was appointed.
proposals.after: An observation commissioner for Ping, Ying, Ying, Mo, and neighboring prefectures was appointed.
proposals.reason: Chinese lists four prefectures 平、營、瀛、莫; the idiomatic English omits 營 (Ying), leaving only three named prefectures.

proposals.before: The observation commissioner for Ping, Ying, Ying, Mo, and other prefectures was established.
proposals.after: The observation commissioner for Ping, Ying (Yingzhou 營), Ying (Yingzhou 瀛), Mo, and other prefectures was established.
proposals.reason: Literal English repeats Ying twice without distinguishing 營 and 瀛, obscuring that two different prefectures are named.

decisions.reason: s0121 names the seized prefectures as 相、衛、洺、貝四州; the idiomatic summary “four of its prefectures” drops those explicit place names. Restoring Xiang, Wei, Ming, and Bei matches the Chinese list and the unit’s literal rendering.
In 幽州節度副使領平盧軍節度副使, 領 marks concurrent tenure of the Pinglu deputy commissionership, not command over that office as an object. “Served as” matches the administrative sense and the idiomatic field.

幽州節度 is the military commissioner (節度使), the person who 兼 holds further posts; rendering the subject as “Youzhou circuit” with “its” misattributes the officeholder. “Military commissioner” and “his” align with the Chinese and the idiomatic field.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 幽州節度兼本軍州經略大使

decisions.after: An observation commissioner for Ping, Ying Prefecture, a second Ying Prefecture, Mo, and neighboring prefectures was appointed.
decisions.reason: 置平、營、瀛、莫等州 lists four prefectures; the idiomatic text omits 營. The proposal’s undifferentiated “Ying, Ying” restores the count but still collapses two distinct places both romanized Ying; marking the latter as a second Ying Prefecture keeps both without Chinese in the English.

decisions.after: The observation commissioner for Ping, Ying Prefecture, a second Ying Prefecture, Mo, and other prefectures was established.
decisions.reason: The literal already has two Ying forms for 營 and 瀛 but does not mark which is which. Calling the latter a second Ying Prefecture distinguishes the two places without Chinese characters or the proposed “Ying (Yingzhou …)” wording.
